So, Mr. Saxon, your re-examination now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Masan, on cross-examination, counsel for the Defence referred to meetings that you had with members of the office of the Prosecution in 1998, as well as meetings in July of this year and more recently. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We need an oral answer. Can you say yes or no, please?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At no time did you ever actually sign any statement provided to you by the Office of the Prosecutor, did you?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You were never shown the contents of any statement or proffer of your testimony, were you?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Awhile ago I received an extract but not recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you ever read back anything from the Office of the Prosecutor in your language?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: In the statements there was some information. When we discussed the statement, some of the information was read back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to adopt the contents of your statement and sign a formal statement of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: No. Nobody suggested what I should say in my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Fila --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is it the position of the Prosecution that the proffers we receive are untrue, incomplete, or both?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon. No. I think what the Prosecutor is saying is that the statements were not signed by the witness. That is what I have understood, but let us hear the response of Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, in response to Mr. O'Sullivan's objection, that is not the position of the Prosecution. At times -- the Defence, at certain times, were trying to have the witness confirm certain details in what were proffers of his testimony, and we're simply trying to clarify the fact that this witness was never -- was never presented with a formal statement to be signed by him and nor did he ever sign any formal statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. O'Sullivan, are you satisfied with the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I heard the answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Continue, Mr. Saxon, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Masan, Mr. Fila asked you some questions about when you saw Mr. Radic standing in the window of the circular staircase the day when beatings occurred in front of the restaurant building. Did those beatings continue until nightfall?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Throughout the period of the distribution of lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Judge Fouad Riad, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Masan, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I will reduce my questions to the minimum, only to the time, but I hope you can give us some more clarification. My first question concerns what happened when Jokic returned the money to the detainees and Krle told him, "You are no longer part of my shift." Now, my first question is what happened to Jokic after that? Was he eliminated completely?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Krle didn't say, "You're no longer in my shift." He said, "You will no longer be in my shift in the future." But the following days Jokic did appear, but he was reserved. He didn't -- he wasn't committed. He acted like a passive observer of events that took place during his shift. He didn't take an active part like the other guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So in other words, he was controlled. He was controlled by Krle.

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: I can't say that he controlled him, but what I can say is that he distanced himself, in a sense, that he wasn't as active as he had been until that incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you said that the detainees rejoiced very much when the money was returned to them by Jokic. They celebrated it. Was it so exceptional that a guard would go against the orders of the commander?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Let me tell you, the money and the amount was not significant. It was an insignificant sum. Twenty-seven billion may have been the equivalent of 100 or 200 German marks, and these were not returned to those who had given them. But this very gesture provoked joy, and the reaction was a brief round of applause amongst us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'll ask you a question concerning Krkan. You said he was present when prisoners were beaten during lunch, if I understood you rightly. Was he present as just a spectator or did he interfere in any way by giving directions either to do or not to do, and when he gave directions, were they obeyed?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: I didn't notice him giving instructions or directly interfering in those activities, but as I said earlier on in my testimony, I noticed him observing things, escorted by at least one person in uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did he participate in any way in the action?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: If I may be allowed to make a conclusion, I think it was a show that was typical of such surroundings, a show of violence, brutality, and brute force. I think that was what that act entailed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I was asking about his role in this show.

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: I think, if I may make conclusions, that he was one of the people watching the show. He was a man who, either for his own pleasure or the pleasure of his escort, had prepared this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You also saw Krkan lead seven people, with a list, and these people -- I mean, this was Halimid, and Juka [sic], and they never returned. Were they led -- did you notice in what direction? Were they led to a bus? Were they being liberated?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Sir, if I may, I should like to correct you. The surname of the man was Baltic, and his nickname was Uca, and a certain gentleman called Halimid. The two of them and another group of five or seven men were escorted by Mladjo Radic, Krkan, in front of this entrance and led in the direction of the "white house." I didn't notice that there was any kind of vehicle there that he could have led them to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And after they were led there, they never showed up again?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: That night there was shooting. There were shouts and cries, "He's escaped," and things like that, so that early in this morning, this mentioned gentlemen, Halimid, we saw him handcuffed and with visible injuries on his face. And after that, no one else showed up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, concerning Mr. Prcac, you mentioned that he would be moving around with paperwork. Did he also carry, like others which you mentioned -- you mentioned that Krle carried stick and cable -- did he carry any instruments, any weapons, or did he look like an administrator?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: I didn't notice him holding any objects or weapons that could be used for mistreatment, but I did notice him carrying lists, and I saw that on a number of occasions, that he himself drew up these lists and called out people and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you hear anybody also calling him "Boss" the way you heard people calling Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: I didn't notice that. I didn't notice it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You noticed that he was giving orders like Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: No. No. The incident I mentioned was something that he himself was involved in, but one of the guards addressed him and said that 50 men were missing, that they were not on the lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Judge Wald, if you please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Just two quick questions, Witness. After Nasic was shot, did you see the guard Pavlic, which you testified fired the shot, did you see him around the camp after that incident?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. And the second question I have was: When was, approximately, the first time, if you can put it in a month or the time of the month, that you saw Prcac around the camp?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Could you even tell whether it was -- let's see, whether it was June or July? Could you even put it in a month?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: I cannot, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only one question following up on the question that Judge Wald put to you. Have you ever seen together, at the same time, Prcac and Kvocka in the camp? Did you ever see them together at the same time?

utterances.speaker: OMER MESAN
utterances.text: Let me see. I would see Prcac before this incident that I described, and I would see him during the daytime, and I would also see Kvocka during the daytime, but I can't say that I saw the two of them together on any one of those days, or I may have forgotten. But it is quite clear that they were there at the same time because they performed their duties during the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Witness. We have finished your testimony. Thank you very much. Let us say once again that we appreciate your courage and honesty regarding the conditions you accepted to testify in, that is, in public, and we wish you a safe journey to your home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon. There are at least from 121 to 127 exhibit numbers to be tendered; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. At this time, the Prosecution would move for the admission of Exhibits 3/121 through 3/127. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was waiting for some explanations but never mind. Mr. Krstan Simic, any objections from the Defence? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. So the mentioned exhibits are admitted into evidence. We have to leave now, so we meet again tomorrow at 9.30, and then, Mr. Keegan, we will be able to hear you. I apologise to the interpreters and all other staff members. I didn't even ask whether they could continue. We did continue, nevertheless, and I thank you all for your understanding for the exceptional circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Wald has suggested to me that perhaps at least we could inquire what is the issue we need to think about to save time tomorrow, and I think that's a good suggestion. So, Mr. Keegan, could you please -- we're not going to have a debate, but just give us an idea what it is about, if possible, and perhaps we can hear, in general terms, the position of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And if we could go into private session as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of September, 2000 at 9.30 a.m.
